newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jailed U.S. official appeals Hong Kong charge.
newsitem.headline: Jailed U.S. official appeals Hong Kong charge.

text.p: A former top U.S. immigration official in Hong Kong who was jailed in connection with a fake passport scheme has appealed, and a prosecutor admitted the man was convicted of the wrong crime.

A spokesman for the Legal Department said on Friday that Jerry Stuchiner, 45, originally appeared in the Court of Appeals on Thursday to ask for a reduction in the 40-month prison term imposed last year.
"The court decided to adjourn the case for a week, until April 25, to enable the applicant to seek legal advice on the case," the spokesman said.

Stuchiner had admitted to a charge of possessing false travel documents and was sentenced last August, but the five fake Honduran passports he carried were blank except for an official chop and signature. By legal definition, a travel document includes a photograph.
Prosecutor Ian McWalters admitted in Thursday's court session that Stuchiner had been convicted of the wrong crime.
Stuchiner changed his appeal against sentence to an appeal against conviction.
Legal experts will consider whether a new trial on fresh charges should be held.

Stuchiner was arrested on July 15 by Hong Kong's Independent Commission Against Corruption working with U.S. Justice Department officials probing a smuggling ring that brought illegal immigrants from Asia to the United States.
